title: Shiv — Discover
description: Stimulating finds beyond the usual queue — economics, institutions, history, and ideas worth sitting with. Private discovery feed for Apple Podcasts.
author: Shivanshu Chaudhary

items.title: A 4-Track Mind (Radiolab)
items.description:
A classic Radiolab short: a neurologist puts a ragtime pianist and a conductor in an fMRI to test a talent that should be impossible — holding multiple complex musical 'tracks' in mind at once.

Watch: https://youtu.be/cEuosugLCVk

Episode: https://radiolab.org/podcast/4-track-mind-2312

items.title: 100 Objects #20: AA Sobriety Chip (99% Invisible)
items.description:
The AA sobriety chip looks like a small token — 99PI digs into the gender, religion, and morality history baked into it.

Watch: https://youtu.be/PJKzCYAWNxA
Episode: https://99percentinvisible.org/?p=48527

items.title: A fall mystery: why do only certain leaves turn red? (Short Wave)
items.description:
NPR Short Wave on why some autumn leaves go red while others stick to yellow — the chemistry and evolutionary bets behind the color show.

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/28/nx-s1-5980105/a-fall-mystery-why-do-only-certain-leaves-turn-red

items.title: Silification Geology (OPALS) with Patrice Rey (Ologies with Alie Ward)
items.description:
Alie Ward with geophysicist Patrice Rey on how opals form, Australian and Ethiopian stones, and the Outback geology behind the flash.

Episode: https://www.alieward.com/ologies/silificationgeology

items.title: What social media gets wrong about inflammation (Short Wave)
items.description:
Short Wave unpacks what inflammation actually is — acute vs chronic — and why social media often blames it for everything from bloating to serious disease.

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/what-social-media-gets-wrong-about-inflammation/id1482575855?i=1000792104396

items.title: How To Avoid The End of the World (Throughline)
items.description:
Throughline revisits how scientists figured out what killed the dinosaurs — and how that discovery shaped how we think about climate, nuclear risk, and avoiding our own catastrophe.

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/10/01/nx-s1-5986020/how-to-avoid-the-end-of-the-world

items.title: How much of Earth's life is still undiscovered? (Short Wave)
items.description:
A new cat species made headlines — and Short Wave asks how rare that really is. Ecologist John Wiens on why we are still discovering life on Earth at an unprecedented pace.

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/30/nx-s1-5978106/new-cat-penguin-species-discovery-biodiversity-genetics

items.title: Is our national debt finally too much? (update) (Planet Money)
items.description:
Planet Money revisits the U.S. national debt with economists Kenneth Rogoff and Karen Dynan — whether we have crossed a dangerous line, and what higher rates mean for what the country can still afford.

Watch: https://youtu.be/mGJRk43YlAw

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/23/nx-s1-5978114/national-debt-rogoff-dynan-red-line

items.title: Who's gonna pay for your Social Security? (Planet Money)
items.description:
Planet Money walks through the main fixes for Social Security’s coming shortfall — whose taxes rise, whose benefits shrink, and what each option actually buys by 2032.

Watch: https://youtu.be/m667oHAa1m4

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/30/nx-s1-5985851/social-security-payment-solutions-retirees

items.title: How two swing states changed American voting
items.description:
Throughline traces how Arizona’s 1960s voter-challenge playbook and Dearborn’s Arab American labor organizing still shape who votes — and who wins — in battleground America.

Watch: https://youtu.be/HleIYu5uwkk

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/17/nx-s1-5969824/how-two-swing-states-changed-american-voting

items.title: Is it time for a Luddite Renaissance? (Throughline)
items.description:
The real Luddites weren’t anti-tech scolds — they were workers fighting machines that threatened their livelihoods. Throughline connects that history to today’s AI anxiety.

Watch: https://youtu.be/TTJzsOJ-X60

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/08/nx-s1-5955618/is-it-time-for-a-luddite-renaissance

items.title: 688. When Is a Bet Not a Bet? (Freakonomics Radio)
items.description:
Part two on prediction markets: Kalshi’s fight with state gambling regulators, and the blurry line between an event contract and a bet — with Gary Gensler, Robin Hanson, and Kalshi’s CEO.

Watch: https://youtu.be/c628dF5qLzA

Episode: https://freakonomics.com/podcast/when-is-a-bet-not-a-bet/

items.title: Forty years of what if (Throughline)
items.description:
Throughline revisits the Challenger disaster through engineer Brian Russell, who spent months warning NASA about freezing temperatures — and has lived with the what-ifs for forty years.

Watch: https://youtu.be/-41SEEhK5SI

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/29/nx-s1-5983667/forty-years-of-what-if

items.title: Tootle of a Devilish Song (99% Invisible)
items.description:
Roman Mars and the 99% Invisible team on how a Swiss mountain call crossed the Atlantic and helped shape the sound of American country music.

Watch: https://youtu.be/Fly-_t49vGc

Episode: https://99percentinvisible.org/?p=48382

items.title: The Sweetest Thing (Radiolab)
items.description:
Latif Nasser’s sons ask what the sweetest thing in the world is — sending him from a West African berry to lab sugar substitutes and a pantry staple that reframes what sweetness even means.

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-sweetest-thing/id152249110?i=1000790523278

items.title: Doves Type (99% Invisible)
items.description:
The story of Doves Type: a legendary typeface, a spectacular friendship breakup, and one extremely committed act of revenge.

Watch: https://youtu.be/ANMExOEG00A

Episode: https://99percentinvisible.org/?p=48765

items.title: How baseball got its beat (Throughline)
items.description:
Throughline on how baseball’s soundtrack was built — organists, walk-up songs, and the sonic rituals that turned a ballpark into a stage.

Watch: https://youtu.be/Ai5HQZ2Fy4U

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/10/nx-s1-5963513/how-baseball-got-its-beat

items.title: 100 Objects #18: Hair Relaxer (99% Invisible)
items.description:
Roman Mars and producer Priscilla Alabi on chemical hair relaxers as design object: Black beauty entrepreneurship, social pressure, and what newer research says about health risk.

Watch: https://youtu.be/znmX0wG9K2A

Episode: https://99percentinvisible.org/episode/100-objects-018-hair-relaxer/

items.title: Grass Apes (Radiolab)
items.description:
Radiolab on how grass remade the planet and us — diet, bodies, and perception — an epic story hiding in the most ordinary plant.

Episode: https://radiolab.org/podcast/grass-apes

items.title: The Disclosure Dilemma: Oversharing (With Leslie John) (Choiceology with Katy Milkman)
items.description:
Katy Milkman with Leslie John on when candid disclosure builds trust — and when holding back costs more than oversharing feels like it will.

Watch: https://youtu.be/dpewTgPmyAQ

Episode: https://schwab.com/learn/story/disclosure-dilemma-oversharing-with-leslie-john

items.title: 100 Objects #19: Western Electric 500 Series (99% Invisible)
items.description:
99% Invisible on the Western Electric 500 Series telephone — the black rotary that once sat in nearly every American home, and what a mass-produced object reveals about design, monopoly, and everyday infrastructure.

Watch: https://youtu.be/jU9P9CR2OsY

Episode: https://99percentinvisible.org/?p=48462

items.title: The Rocky Statue (99% Invisible)
items.description:
99% Invisible on how a movie prop became a civic monument in Philadelphia — and how the crowd’s claim beat the art establishment over what represents a place.

Watch: https://youtu.be/PcpttgVTlIQ

Episode: https://99percentinvisible.org/episode/684-the-rocky-statue/

items.title: Middlegarchs are the new Oligarchs (Planet Money)
items.description:
Planet Money on “middlegarchs”: stealth millionaires who shape markets without oligarch-scale brand gravity — a clearer map of soft power in the middle of the wealth distribution.

Watch: https://youtu.be/_y8FrkZXvXA

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/25/nx-s1-5981194/stealthy-wealthy-everywhere-millionaires-pass-through

items.title: Democratic Socialism. Hope or Hopeless? (Throughline)
items.description:
Throughline on Michael Harrington’s path from Catholic radical to Democratic loyalist — when compromise builds power, and when it dissolves the movement.

Watch: https://youtu.be/5NbIJDnGkqQ

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/24/nx-s1-5979087/democratic-socialism-hope-or-hopeless

items.title: Gita Gopinath on Trade, Currencies, and Economic Transformation (Conversations with Tyler)
items.description:
Tyler Cowen with IMF deputy MD Gita Gopinath on dollar dominance, sovereign debt plumbing, and how currencies reshape trade and economic transformation.

Watch: https://youtu.be/MPXd2pa5V9Y

Episode: https://cowenconvos.libsyn.com/gita-gopinath-on-trade-currencies-and-economic-transformation

items.title: Jared Diamond on Leaders, Luck, and Irreplaceability (Conversations with Tyler)
items.description:
Tyler Cowen with Jared Diamond on leaders, luck, and irreplaceability — when individuals actually move history across prophets, CEOs, and coaches.

Watch: https://youtu.be/SwcVPrH_waU

Episode: https://conversationswithtyler.com/episodes/jared-diamond/

items.title: 687. Are Prediction Markets the Best Forecasting Tool Ever — or Just Another Casino? (Freakonomics Radio)
items.description:
Freakonomics Radio on prediction markets: best forecasting tool ever, or sports-bet liquidity dressed as civic tech — and how Kalshi and experts frame “information” vs entertainment.

Watch: https://youtu.be/UDyQLVhGiIY

Episode: https://freakonomics.com/podcast/are-prediction-markets-the-best-forecasting-tool-ever-or-just-another-casino/

items.title: The loan at the heart of a new foreclosure crisis (Planet Money)
items.description:
Planet Money on DSCR loans: rental cash-flow underwriting that scales investor portfolios — and how one Baltimore stack shows GFC-style risk returning under a new label.

Watch: https://youtu.be/JcBRR4ftTQE

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-loan-at-the-heart-of-a-new-foreclosure-crisis/id290783428?i=1000789070345

items.title: The Domino’s Pizza Tracker Theory of Everything (Planet Money)
items.description:
Planet Money on the Domino’s pizza tracker as labor illusion — progress UI that makes waiting feel like work being done, and the economics hiding in a pizza app.

Watch: https://youtu.be/r2oo0u2Zpdw

Episode: https://www.npr.org/2026/09/18/nx-s1-5974101/dominos-pizza-tracker-labor-illusion

items.title: Talent, Time and Money: The Curse of General Magic (Cautionary Tales with Tim Harford)
items.description:
Cautionary Tales on General Magic: talent, nearly unlimited cash, and a fifteen-year head start on the smartphone — and why constraints, not abundance, often decide who wins.

Watch: https://youtu.be/JE7XMevEFTg

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/talent-time-and-money-the-curse-of-general-magic/id1484511465?i=1000788891693

items.title: Annie Lowrey on the Time Tax, Fraud, and Rationing by Paperwork (Conversations with Tyler)
items.description:
Tyler Cowen with Annie Lowrey on the time tax: hours spent on hold, in waiting rooms, and filling forms — and whether bureaucracy is a regressive levy or a quiet rationing tool.

Watch: https://youtu.be/o0ZDf0bgEXE

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/annie-lowrey-on-the-time-tax-fraud-and-rationing/id983795625?i=1000790017400

items.title: 706. Queen Victoria’s Revenge: Storming the Citadel (Part 2) (The Rest Is History)
items.description:
The Rest Is History concludes Queen Victoria’s Abyssinian expedition: Napier’s rescue of European hostages, the storming of Magdala, and one of the empire’s most epic campaigns.

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/queen-victorias-revenge-storming-the-citadel-part-2/id1537788786?i=1000789062489&uo=4

items.title: Incentives Are for Losers (with Adam Mastroianni) (EconTalk)
items.description:
EconTalk with Adam Mastroianni: when following bad incentives is “loser behavior” — and why figuring out right from wrong yourself is harder than maximizing the scoreboard.

Watch: https://youtu.be/XEislRTN_F8

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/incentives-are-for-losers-with-adam-mastroianni/id135066958?i=1000789541014

items.title: Show 74 - Mania for Subjugation IV (Hardcore History)
items.description:
Dan Carlin’s Hardcore History on the Battle of Issus — Alexander versus Persia’s Great King in a showdown often skipped by Hollywood but decisive in ancient history.

Watch: https://youtu.be/Gu4syP_IzQs

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/mania-for-subjugation-iv/id173001861?i=1000779313976
